coupling: The first commit introduces a 32-bit output-capacity representation for compressed IDManifest decompression, but validates it against the full 64-bit uncompressed size and uses the same narrow value for both allocation and decompression, so that commit is safe by itself. The later bounds commit replaces that absolute 32-bit ceiling with the intended compression-ratio check, which legitimately accepts sizes above 4 GiB, while retaining the wrapped 32-bit allocation and passing the now-validated full 64-bit size to the decompressor. The resulting heap buffer is smaller than the capacity advertised to libdeflate, so a ratio-compliant stream writes past the allocation. A reviewer must trace the capacity representation introduced by the first commit through the later validation change; treating either commit as an isolated maintenance change misses the mismatch.
